name: Cornerless Recovery Requires a Maximal Layer Set
statement: If a nonempty layer set $E$ satisfies the singleton recovery criterion for an ample family $X$ and its recovered seed $X^E$ is cornerless, then no proper superset of $E$ also satisfies that criterion. If $X$ is an irredundantly embedded ample forbidden pc-minor and $E$ is maximal among its successful layer sets, then $X^E$ has no nonempty successful layer set and no thin coordinate; it is a forbidden pc-minor with at least two one-concept repairs in the dismantlable ample class, but it need not be cornerless. Consequently, $X$ has a successful recovery with cornerless seed exactly when $E_{\max}(X)$ exists and $X^{E_{\max}(X)}$ is cornerless.
proof: Suppose a proper successful superset $D$ existed. Recover the signed-facet presentation over $D$ and strongly project its rows along $E$. Every row owning a facet in $D\setminus E$ survives as a product of a singly punctured cube with a cube, and at least one survives because every signed facet outside $E$ has an owner. A corner of such a row lifts to a corner of $X^E$, contradicting cornerlessness. If instead $E$ is maximal for a forbidden obstruction, any successful layer set in $X^E$ would enlarge $E$ by nested recovery. Obstruction descent makes $X^E$ forbidden, while the two distinct owners of either sign at any layer coordinate give two repairs. A thin seed coordinate would itself be a successful singleton. Union closure makes the maximal successful set unique and gives the final equivalence.
comments: Maximality of the layer set eliminates further recoverable layers, but it does not force the recovered obstruction itself to be cornerless.
